title: Civil War and the Near Destruction of Benjamin

date.label: Undated Judges narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Judges 20 describes a war between an Israelite coalition and Benjamin
claims.evidence: Judges 20:12–48 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). All the children of Israel go out and gather as one man, from Dan to Beersheba with the land of Gilead, to the LORD at Mizpah; the Levite gives his account of the crime, and the tribes demand that Benjamin surrender the men of Gibeah. Benjamin refuses, and fighting follows: heavy Israelite losses in the first two engagements (twenty-two thousand men the first day, eighteen thousand the second), then a final reversal that devastates Benjamin, burns its cities, and leaves only six hundred men who flee to the rock Rimmon. Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated. The figures are narrative figures, not casualty totals independently verified by excavation.

claims.claim: Judges 21 depicts coerced acquisition of women after an oath crisis
claims.evidence: Judges 21:8–23 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). An oath sworn at Mizpah against giving daughters to Benjamin, combined with the tribe's near destruction, creates a crisis over its survival. Judges 21:18 recalls the sworn curse: "Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin." To preserve the tribe, the people attack Jabesh-gilead and take four hundred women who had not known a man (21:10–12), and arrange for Benjaminites to seize women dancing at the yearly feast of the LORD at Shiloh (21:19–23). The text records no consent from the women of Jabesh-gilead or Shiloh; the four hundred are not enough — six hundred Benjaminites survive — and the shortfall is the reason the Shiloh seizure is arranged. The oath is grounded in Judges 21:18, inside this claim's passage (21:8–23). Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

claims.claim: Phinehas is named as a priest in the inquiry episode
claims.evidence: Judges 20:28 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Judges 20:28 names Phinehas son of Eleazar as ministering before the ark of the covenant at the second inquiry (20:26–28), after two defeats, accompanied by weeping, fasting, and burnt offerings and peace offerings. The same Phinehas appears in Numbers 25 and Joshua 22. The reference gives the episode no agreed external date; the text does not say when the war happened, and no external evidence fixes it. Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

review.notes: Proposed unpublished Judges category; source access remains limited and audit restrictions apply. Phase 4 readiness and independent QA are distinct. No editorial override needed: S026 is not listed in sources[] (J01–J11 precedent); all 3 sources in sources[] are verified. JCL-12-004 is EXCLUDED from published factual claims (J02/JCL-02-003 + J08/JCL-08-004 precedent): the registry instruction is "EXCLUDE from published factual claims; retain audit ID and rationale." The registry's corrected_wording ("Judges 20 reports casualties, but archaeology cannot independently verify these numbers or identify battle participants") is the exclusion rationale, not a claim — no claim is built from it. The prose keeps the substance ("Archaeology does not independently confirm the precise casualties in Judges 20: the figures in the chapter are narrative figures, and no destruction layer can be read as a casualty list."). Mapping: clm-jud-12-001–003 are JCL-12-001–003; JCL-12-004 is excluded. JADD-006 is implemented in the prose, NOT as a separate claim: JADD-006 (Judg 20:18,26–28) is a REVISE item — the Bethel/KJV rendering note + a 5-way split (20:1; 20:18; 20:26–28; 21:12; 21:19 — never build as 20:18–28). The draft's "Mizpah, Bethel, and Shiloh" subsection keeps the three places separate (Mizpah 20:1, Bethel 20:18 + 20:26–28, Shiloh 21:12 + 21:19), the two Bethel inquiries are NOT collapsed into one (20:18 before the first battle, 20:26–28 after two defeats), and the Hebrew bêt-ʾēl + the KJV "house of God" rendering are given together (a reader checking the stored KJV text would not find the word "Bethel" there). D-J12-1 is RESOLVED by grounding change (NOT passage widening): Step 5 found the draft citing Judges 21:1 ("Judges 21:1 says Israel swore at Mizpah not to give daughters to Benjamin"), outside JCL-12-002's passage (21:8–23). The draft grounds the oath in Judg 21:18 instead ("Judges 21:18 recalls the sworn curse: 'Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin.'"), which is INSIDE JCL-12-002's passage — the 21:1 citation is gone. The second reader confirms: "The oath is re-grounded in Judg 21:18 (inside JCL-12-002's passage); the Overview's 'An oath sworn at Mizpah' carries no verse number and is chapter narrative summary — correctly left." The claim passage stays 21:8–23 (NO widening). S026 is NOT in sources[] (J01–J11 precedent): S026 (source-biblical-texts-canonical-cross-references) is not-independently-verified (Partial — cross-referenced verses read only where covered by the S001/S009 reads; no systematic read of the cited passages). It is listed in the registry for all 4 connections, but claims and connections carry no per-item source lists in the category JSON, so its connection role does not require it in sources[]. S026 is not cited in the J12 prose at all. No internal research IDs (JCL-/JADD-) appear in the reader-facing prose (the draft already contained none), and the prose is kept precise to what the claims state (the numbers in Judges 20 are narrative figures, not excavation totals; Edenburg's composition argument is attributed, never consensus; the women of Jabesh-gilead and Shiloh are presented as not consenting). Three process-facing sentences were reworded ("The claim that archaeology independently confirms the precise casualties in Judges 20 is excluded from this corpus, and this paragraph correctly refuses it"; "so the claim must carry the Hebrew and the rendering together"; "in the grounding pass").
